research_concepts: PNR fail as a trigger condition
methodological_questions: How is 'PNR fail' defined without conditioning on the outcome being measured?
What is the unit (team, opponent, lineup, defender, or possession chain), and how many units exist with adequate PULL_UP exposure after a PNR fail?
What baseline defines lift, and is it matched on shot quality, opponent, and game context?
Does the >=70% share of positive-lift units with median lift >2pp need a null distribution and multiplicity control?

historical_evidence.finding: Descriptive RS vs playoff comparison across 25 defensive teams (min 30 possessions per cell). PULL_UP PPP allowed rose +0.341 with share -7.6pp. The record notes no inferential test and that the PNR share jump of +12.1pp may reflect tagging differences.

Named-star lineup and forced-play-type suppressors (e.g., Giannis forced PULL_UP PPP 0.848, -0.540 vs preferred DRIVE). The record notes no placebo or matching, and that later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts.
Superstar suppression profiles. Rank-1 suppressor deltas vary by player, with most within 1-2 SE and no multiple-comparison control. The record flags an OTHER artifact.
TOV_FORCE matchup decomposition on four playoff games. Team-PT lifts are small (including PNR lifts of -4.1pp and +1.2pp). Player-channel lifts are large but based on small cells (n often 15-54).

Raw channel lifts shrink by about 50% or more after opponent re-route and PT-shift adjustments. The record states net lift is model-implied rather than observed, and that the surrogate is often additive at n<10.
On-ball scheme labels populated at 14.9% (DET) and 3.3% (ORL) of on-ball possessions. The switches_on field was unpopulated.

Adaptation falsification tests were flagged as an artifact (C_artifact), limited by label or classification error and selection or regression to the mean. Risks recorded: LABEL_ERROR and MECHANICAL_FLOOR.
Within-game adaptation toward counters showed an adapter PPP advantage that was limited by selection or regression to the mean. The record also shows a SWITCH subgroup reversal.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labelling on-ball defensive coverage from NBA matchup and play-by-play fields to support counter analysis
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable: confident label rates were 14.9% and 3.3%, and switches_on was not populated, so the coverage conditioning variable was not usable at scale.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Player-channel matchup lift decomposition on four playoff games
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable: cells had n often 15-54, primary_defender attribution included helper steals, and there was no holdout or game-outcome check.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Surviving-lift test for TOV_FORCE channels after re-routing and PT-shift adjustment
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as E_unclear: net lift was model-implied rather than observed, with about 4 games and 8 offense-defense sides, and R3 was often an additive surrogate at n<10.

failed_approaches.what_failed: A1 adaptation asymmetry, confidence and carryover tests
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact: the apparent effect was attributed to label or classification error and selection or regression to the mean (LABEL_ERROR and MECHANICAL_FLOOR risks).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Star lineup and forced-play-type suppression claims without placebo or matching
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as E_unclear: no placebo or matching, and later sequence work treated similar gaps as artifacts (PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE risk).

evidence_establishes: Earlier project work on this data has repeatedly produced play-type PPP gaps (including PULL_UP-related gaps in SF-APPS-012 and SF-CHT-009), but none tested a league-wide, unit-level PNR-fail-then-PULL_UP counter claim.
Several related inferential efforts were flagged as artifacts or inconclusive, mainly because of label error, regression to the mean, small cells, and missing placebo controls.
Attempts to condition on defensive scheme or coverage labels failed on label coverage in the retrieved records.
The retrieved records do not show a validated definition of PNR fail or a validated unit-level lift estimator.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether a PNR-fail-to-PULL_UP lift is positive in >=70% of units, or whether its median exceeds 2pp.
Whether PULL_UP's PPP advantage after PNR fail survives matching on shot quality, opponent, and game context.
Any estimate of unit-level lift variance, because no such unit-level analysis is recorded.
Whether the PNR share and tagging differences in SF-APPS-012 affect a PNR-conditioned analysis.
Anything about the 2025-26 regular season or playoff data, since no record covers those files.
own_inferences: The question as posed is not operational: 'PNR fail' is not defined, and 'units' is not defined. If fail is defined by low possession PPP, the conditioning is outcome-derived and the lift is mechanically tied to the definition.
The threshold of 70% of units with lift >0 and median lift >2pp has no null reference. Under noise alone, a share of positive units can be high when baseline PULL_UP is efficient.

Because PULL_UP is a shot type with fixed mechanics, a positive lift can reflect shot-quality differences rather than a defensive counter. This needs comparison on expected PPP from shot distance and type.
Units with adequate PNR-fail and PULL_UP exposure are likely a small fraction of teams and seasons, so a league-wide claim probably rests on few units.
uncertainties: The exact definition of PNR fail, the unit definition, and the baseline are not given in the task, and no retrieved record defines them.
No retrieved record reports unit-level exposure counts for PNR-fail possessions.
The data version for 2025-26 is partial before 2026-04-13 (regular season) and 2026-06-21 (playoffs). Using partial data would introduce drift and incomplete-season bias.
Retrieval returned no record of a validated defensive-matchup or PNR-fail definition, so the historical evidence is indirect.
Whether the historical records' statuses reflect the full data or subsets is not stated.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records show that earlier counter-type and matchup-lift analyses on this data were flagged as artifact, untestable, or non-hypothesis-test, mainly from label coverage, exposure sparsity, selection or regression to the mean, and missing placebos. Those outcomes make a direct proceed unjustified. The decision moved from a possible proceed toward do_not_proceed as posed, with a minimum viable pre-specified test described below.

blocking_constraints.text: PNR 'fail' is not defined. If defined by low PPP or turnover on the same possession, the conditioning is outcome-derived and lift is partly built in.
Units selected for PNR failure on a bad outcome will regress toward their means, so a positive PULL_UP lift may be a regression artifact (see SF-APPA-001 and SF13).
Few units will have enough PNR-fail followed by PULL_UP possessions for stable unit-level lift (see SF-APPA-066 n 15-54).
A 2pp median lift threshold across units needs far more possessions per unit than the per-game files provide for most units (see SF-APPS-058 and SF-APPA-004).
Play-type and defensive-scheme labels are inferred from play-by-play and matchup fields with low coverage (see SF-APPS-058, SF-APPA-001).

prior_work.summary: Earlier records touch the PULL_UP-after-PNR question only indirectly. SF-APPS-012 and SF-CHT-009 report PULL_UP PPP gaps without inferential control. SF-APPM-022 reports suppression profiles that are mostly within 1-2 SE and not multiplicity-corrected. SF-APPA-067 and SF-APPA-001 show that lift shrinks or becomes artifactual under adjustment. No retrieved record tests the stated unit-level counter claim with the stated threshold.

risks.text: PNR fail defined on the outcome being evaluated (PPP or turnover) makes the conditioning circular.
Selecting possessions or units on failure inflates apparent PULL_UP lift through regression to the mean.
Shot quality, shot distance, opponent defender, and lineup differences can drive PULL_UP PPP independent of any counter effect.
Lift can be mechanically positive if the PNR-fail baseline is depressed by the definition of fail.
Unit-level lift threshold of 2pp with a 70% share has no power analysis; unit counts and per-unit possessions are likely too low.
Many units will have too few PNR-fail then PULL_UP possessions for estimation.
Testing PULL_UP across many play types and units, or re-running after failed definitions, inflates false positives (see SF-APPM-022).
PNR and PULL_UP tagging, and any defensive-scheme labels, may be misclassified (see SF-APPS-058 and SF-APPS-012 tagging note).
Without placebo play types or placebo units, the lift cannot be separated from baseline play-type efficiency (see SF-CHT-009).
Mixing regular season and playoff data, and partial 2025-26 files, changes defensive tendencies and tagging over time (see SF-APPS-012).
Unit-level PPP lift from small possession counts has low reliability and may not replicate across seasons.

methodological_questions: Is PULL_UP lift after PNR fail positive across units?
What share of units show lift greater than 0 and median lift above 2pp?
How should unit-level lift be estimated and aggregated for counter strategy claims?
args.query: PNR fail followed by PULL_UP shot counter strategy lift across units, defensive suppression, best and avoid counter analysis

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-05-23, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter, it should show lift>0 in >=70% of units with median lift>2pp.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
